issue.body:
The current implementation in #1337 has no exception for `try`, `else`, `finally`, do`.

Having `space-after-keywords` and `space-after-block` both on will raise errors like this:

``` sh
34:4  error  Keyword "try" must be followed by whitespace  space-after-keywords
34:7  error  Missing space before opening brace            space-before-blocks
```

This is lousy because it means these two rules need to be configured the same, otherwise they will give opposing information. I'd like to figure out which rule should be the canonical home for this warning and remove it from the other.

body:
~~`else` is handled by space-before-blocks.~~

See [#1338 (comment)](https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/1338#issuecomment-139918022) - `else{` is covered right now by space-after-keywords and space-before-blocks. I elaborate more in that comment, but my earlier suggestion could solve both of these issues.
We can just skip if the block is the body of an arrow function.

issue.body:
Fixes #3769.
I made `space-before-blocks` ignoring spacing which is between `=>` and `{`.

I don't address #1338 in this PR.
I thought it can resolve #1338 that to ignore spacing merely if the previous token is a keyword.
But `class` keywords are not handled by `space-after-keywords`, so we need think about a ClassExpression `var Foo = class{ };`.

BTW, 72 is too short to include two rule names...
